role: class of permitted semantic data of a semantics
notes: Members are the complete tuples of the semantics \(\mathcal S\): a valuation, a structure-assignment pair, or a Kripke structure-world pair in the three instances.
A member of \(\mathcal D_{\mathcal S}\); local metavariable, not a domain element.

role: satisfaction of a formula by a datum of a named semantics
notes: Instance of the registered per-system pattern \(\models_{S}\); with a set operand, satisfaction of every member. The global \(v\models\varphi\), \(\mathcal M,s\models\varphi\) and \(\mathcal M,w\models A\) rows are its three instances.
Inherited source notation of ch. Structures, Satisfaction, and Translation; sends \(x\) to \(a\) and agrees with \(s\) elsewhere. Not substitution.

role: value of a term in a structure under an assignment
notes: Inherited source term-value notation, used here in the atomic satisfaction clauses.

role: valuation extending a finite partial valuation by F
notes: \(u\colon P\to\mathbb B\) for finite \(P\subseteq\mathsf{Prop}\); \(u^{+}\) agrees with \(u\) on \(P\) and is \(\mathbf F\) elsewhere.

role: source CPL truth-value set and values
notes: Same typed role as the registered rows scoped to P2 prop-syntax-semantics; this row extends their scope to this section.

role: local modal consequence over a frame class
notes: Same typed role as the registered row scoped to P8 modal-temporal-epistemic; used in this section for the modal instance of consequence over whole tuples.

Worlds, accessibility relation, valuation \(\mathsf{Prop}\to\mathcal P(W)\); same typed roles as the registered P8 rows. \(R\) is the accessibility relation only inside the modal clauses; elsewhere in the section \(R\) is a unary relation symbol.

role: set of formulas with an open assumption occurrence in a derivation
notes: Defined for natural-deduction derivations of ND_CPL and ND_FOL; open means undischarged.

role: last rule application of a derivation and the formulas it discharges
notes: \(\Delta_\rho\) is the set of formulas of which \(\rho\) discharges at least one occurrence; it is a formula set, not a context.
Local metavariables for derivation trees in the statements and annex proofs.
